problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to service six distinct facilities, each positioned at specific grid coordinates on a regional map:
Facility Alpha: Coordinates (123,90)
Facility Beta: Coordinates (156,73)
Facility Gamma: Coordinates (172,91)
Facility Delta: Coordinates (151,162)
Facility Epsilon: Coordinates (158,33)
Facility Zeta: Coordinates (183,79)

The travel distances, measured in kilometers, between pairs of facilities are predetermined:
Alpha to Gamma: 49.0 km
Alpha to Delta: 77.3 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 66.9 km
Alpha to Zeta: 61.0 km
Beta to Gamma: 24.1 km
Beta to Delta: 89.1 km
Beta to Epsilon: 40.0 km
Beta to Zeta: 27.7 km
Gamma to Delta: 74.0 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 59.7 km
Gamma to Zeta: 16.3 km
Delta to Epsilon: 129.2 km
Delta to Zeta: 89.0 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 52.4 km

Due to infrastructural limitations, direct travel between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta is not possible. Furthermore, a specific routing mandate requires that exactly one of two critical connections must be incorporated into the circuit: either the link between Facility Beta and Gamma, or the link between Facility Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-loop itinerary, where the technician visits each facility precisely once before returning to the point of origin, thereby minimizing the total distance traversed.
